sentences.text: Dallasiella was a shark belonging to the class Chondrichthyes, a group of cartilaginous fish.
It is placed within the parent group Lamniformes, though its exact family position remains uncertain.
The genus Dallasiella was described by Cappetta and Case in 1999.
The type species is Dallasiella willistoni, and the genus contains two valid species: Dallasiella brachyodon and Dallasiella willistoni.
Dallasiella is currently classified as Lamniformes incertae sedis, having previously been placed in the families Cretoxyrhinidae and Archaeolamnidae.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous period, spanning from the Albian to the Campanian stages.
Its existence is dated between 113.2 and 72.2 million years ago.
Fossils of Dallasiella species have been found in North America and Europe.
